Below is a quick reference guide so you can send your “malicious” verdict for **IP 22.242.75.136** yourself from the command line or within a script.  
(If you’re working inside a programming environment like Python, just adapt the snippet below.)

---

### 1️⃣ What you’ll need  

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| `API_KEY` – your *“key_four”* value | Authenticates you against the VT API |
| Target IP | `22.242.75.136` |
| Verdict JSON | `{ "type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"} }` |

> ⚠️ Make sure you keep your API key secret—don’t commit it into public repos!

---

### 2️⃣ Endpoint & Method  

```
POST https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/votes
Content-Type: application/json
x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>
```

---

### 3️⃣ Example Commands  

#### • Using `curl`

```bash
curl -X POST \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "x-apikey: $KEY_FOUR" \
     --data '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}' \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/votes
```

Replace `$KEY_FOUR` with your real key.

#### • In Python (`requests`)  

```python
import requests

api_key   = "<your-key-four>"
ip_addr   = "22.242.75.136"
url       = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip_addr}/votes"

payload   = {
    "type": "vote",
    "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" }
}

headers = {
    "accept": "application/json",
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "x-apikey": api_key,
}

response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)

print(response.status_code)          # Expect 200 OK / 201 Created
print(response.json())               # Response body
```

---

### 4️⃣ Things to Keep in Mind  

| Tip | Explanation |
|-----|-------------|
| **Rate limits** | VT enforces per‑minute quotas. If you hit them, wait before retrying. |
| **Idempotency** | Submitting the same vote twice will simply overwrite the previous one. |
| **Response handling** | A successful call returns status codes `200`, `201`, or `204`. Errors come back with useful messages under `"error"` → `"message"`. |
| **Logging** | Store the response somewhere secure; it’s handy for audit trails. |

---

That’s all! Once you run the above, VirusTotal will register your “malicious” flag for that IP address. Let me know if you’d like help parsing the response or automating this across multiple IPs.
